problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+y\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $y=2{sin}^{2}⁡x$ traversed from the point $A(0,0)$ to the point $B(\frac{\pi }{2},2).$
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Since $y$ is the subject of the equation, a parametrization is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =t\,i+2{sin}^{2}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le \frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y=2{sin}^{2}⁡t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2{sin}^{2}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{sin}^{2}⁡t)j \\  & =i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2{sin}^{2}⁡t\text{ })\cdot (i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8{sin}^{3}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8{sin}^{3}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,dt \\  & ={[\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2{sin}^{4}⁡t]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
